Definition: from G2532 and G1563; likewise in that place:--and there, there (thither) also.
BiblicalUsage: Kakei is 'and there' — the word that moves the scene along. If thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; into whatsoever city ye shall enter, and there abide till ye go thence; and Jesus walked no more openly among the Jews, but went thence into a country near the wilderness, and there continued with His disciples.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that 'and there' reminds me God meets us in places: at the altar, in the city, in the wilderness near Ephraim — and the place matters because He is there.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
